purpose: diagnose the owner's report that the second player stopped moving in the Godot padel port
state: Symptom: second player stops moving. Stored profile playerMode=coop, default solo. Port: _second_human() = state.pvp or state.coop (match_controller.gd:1253); partner fed by the second sampler, pad-only (input_map.gd:31-33, 262-265), NO_DEVICE without a second pad (assign_devices, :357-364); sim.gd:2457 update_doubles_ai moves the partner with the AI only if not state.coop; coop drives the mate from the human struct (sim.gd:2778-2786, :3030). Reference: getInput2() reads gamepad2 only (js/main.js:1096-1122); pmHint says two controllers (js/i18n.js:1268); default playerMode solo (js/ui.js:476). Measured probe, 20 s per mode: solo partner moved 859 frames / rally 9; coop partner moved 0 frames, 3 serve jumps, travel 304 / rally 1; pvp second human's side moved 0 / rally 0. Machine: one Xbox pad, no second controller.

questions.explained: noul: is coop + one controller sufficient to account for the still second player with no second unexplained cause in the code path
questions.remedy: choice: what should the port do when co-op/versus is selected with no second controller (parity_nothing / parity_plus_state / gate_the_buttons / ai_fallback / other)
questions.blocking: score: how much should this hold up shipping the build (0 not a blocker .. 3 blocks the release)

used_for: Confirmed the diagnosis as sufficient (0.76) so the finding is reported as the owner's setup rather than as a code regression, and kept the remedy out of the code: the low-confidence split (0.41 on 'parity plus a live controller indicator', confidence 0.26, with 'parity only' 0.23 and 'gate the buttons' 0.21 close behind) matches the standing rule that a UI fork is the owner's verdict, so the three options were recorded in the evidence file for him instead of being built. The 1.03 score kept this out of the release-blocking class.
